Check that two tables cannot be subtracted

check_differencing.Rd

A differencing attack subtracts two released tables to reveal a small group: a table for all persons and one for all persons except one settlement differ by exactly that settlement. The check compares counts cell by cell on the shared grouping variables and also compares the grand totals. It fails if any difference is between 1 and min_count - 1.

Usage

check_differencing(x, y, by = NULL, count = NULL, config = NULL, target = NULL)

Arguments

x, y

Aggregated tables (data frames with a count column, or tables).

by

Grouping variables shared by both tables. Defaults to the non-numeric columns they have in common.

count

Name of the count column, the same in both tables. Detected automatically when possible.

config

A mimic_config(); NULL uses the defaults.

target

Label used in reports.

Value

A mimic_check. details lists the groups whose difference is small.

See also

Other checks: check_dominance(), check_extremes(), check_group_disclosure(), check_k_anonymity(), check_keys(), check_min_count(), check_model(), check_suppression()

Examples

all <- as.data.frame(table(sex = fake_persons$sex))
most <- as.data.frame(table(sex = fake_persons$sex[fake_persons$settlement != "Settlement_20"]))
check_differencing(all, most)
#> ✖ differencing (all vs most): Subtracting the tables reveals fewer than 5 persons in 1 cell(s) and the grand totals.
#>  sex
#>    F
